full_judgment: his examination in cross that he culltivates western half of the suit land but he could not say dag number and khatian number. He further says that there is dispute in respect of eastern half of the suit-land. He also says that Abdul jabbar harvested paddy of the eastern half D.W.4 is another bargadar, he also could not say dag number of the suit land. He says that he cultivates eastern half of the suit land as bargader the other bargadar sharafat said that Abdul Jabbar hervested crops from the eastern half. The learned lower court did not discuss the entire evidence on the point of possession but on the basis of single statement held that the plaintiff was not in possession. The learned appellate court after discussing the evidence found the decision given by the trial court on the basis of a single statement was not proper. The appellate court also found that the plaintiff contracted to purchases only 5 decimal out of 88 decimals of plot No. 3952 which is pond. It is obvious that there are other co-sharers of that pond. D.W4 says that Abdul Momin Chowdhury had a share in that pond. Naturally, Abdul Momin Chowdhury caught fish on that particular dated. So, it is clear that the learned lower court arrived at a decision on the question of possession without discussing the entire evidence on record. On the other hand, on consideration of the evidence on record, it appears to me that the learned appellate court was not wrong when decided that the plaintiff proved his possession in the suit land.
